title: Electronic Tongue Generating Continuous Recognition Patterns for Protein Analysis
protocol: Prepare 100 ml of phosphate buffer solution (PBS-G) containing 50 mM NaH2PO4, 50 mM NaCl, and 10% glycerol at pH 6.8.
Prepare 250 ml of HEPES buffer solution containing 10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% Tween 20 at pH 7.4.
Prepare stock solution of building block 1 (BB1) lactose and building block 2 (BB2) sulfated lactose at 0.2 mM in PBS-G.
Prepare 1 ml of protein solutions in HEPES: Arachis hypogaea lectin (AHL) at 500 nM, myoglobin at 1 µM, and lysozyme at 500 nM.
Prepare 20 ml of 1% SDS in ultrapure water.
Clean the gold surface of the prism 48 hr prior to use with a plasma cleaner for 3 min under conditions: 75% Oxygen, 25% Argon, 0.6 mbar, power 40 W.
Prepare eleven pure and mixed solutions of BB1 and BB2 with [BB1]/([BB1]+[BB2]) ratios between 0 and 100% by increments of 10% at a total BB concentration of 0.1 mM in PBS-G.
Deposit 8 nl droplets of these pure and mixed solutions on the prism surface using a non-contact spotter in quadruplicate for each ratio with 44 spots in total.
Place the prism inside a Petri dish containing 1 ml of ultrapure water.
Leave the prism overnight at room temperature for self-assembly of BB1 and BB2 on the gold surface.
Wash the prism thoroughly with ultrapure water.
Dry the prism under a flow of argon.
Set the incubator in which the SPRi apparatus is placed to 25 °C.
Insert a non-functionalized rinsing prism in the PEEK flow cell connected to a computer-controlled syringe pump, degasser, and medium pressure injection valve.
Fill the flow system with freshly filtered and degassed running buffer HEPES.
Remove the rinsing prism from the flow cell.
Insert the prism containing the CoCRR array into the flow cell.
Run HEPES at a 100 µl/min flow rate.
Pass running buffer quickly to remove any air bubbles present on the prism surface with the help of a CCD camera.
Define study area for each spot by drawing a circle with the same diameter as the area of interest based on a well-contrasted image of the array using integrated software in SPRi system.
Trace plasmon curves, which represent reflectivity curves in function of the incident angle, for all spots.
Choose the working angle with the highest slope on reflectivity curves.
Rotate the scanning mirror to fix the selected working angle.
Continue running HEPES through the flow system until the reflectivity signal stabilizes.
Load 1 ml of AHL solution into the sample loop (500 µl).
Put the injection valve to the "injection" position.
Monitor reflectivity variations against time simultaneously on all spots during protein injection.
Rinse the array with running buffer for 8 min after protein injection ends.
Inject 1 ml of 1% SDS to regenerate the array.
Repeat the procedure for other proteins.
Plot the reflectivity (R%) at the end of each protein injection versus the [BB1]/([BB1]+[BB2]) ratio using a math computing software.
